data.title: Whole-body phototherapy (cabin NB-UVB ± PUVA)
data.summary: Cabin NB-UVB and PUVA: dosing, protection, missed doses, logs, stopping
data.body:
Whole-body phototherapy treats patients standing in a cabin lined with UV tubes. NB-UVB (311 nm) is first line; PUVA (oral psoralen plus UVA) is reserved for thick or resistant disease. Safe practice depends on careful dosing and record-keeping.

## Indications
- Psoriasis involving more than ~10% body surface area, or resistant to topicals
- Generalised vitiligo (NB-UVB is first line)
- Atopic dermatitis, generalised pruritus, prurigo
- Mycosis fungoides (patch / thin plaque: NB-UVB; thicker plaque: PUVA)
- PLE prophylaxis, lichen planus, pityriasis lichenoides

## Contraindications
- Absolute: XP, photosensitive lupus, porphyria, history of melanoma; PUVA: pregnancy, breastfeeding, children under 12 (for oral psoralen)
- Relative: multiple NMSC, photosensitising drugs, immunosuppressants, cataract, liver disease (PUVA), claustrophobia, unable to stand for several minutes
- NB-UVB is acceptable in pregnancy (consider folate supplement)

## Pre-procedure
- Consent: long course, 2–3 visits per week; erythema, itching, tanning; skin-cancer and cataract risk with PUVA
- Determine skin type (Fitzpatrick) and, if available, **MED** (NB-UVB) or **MPD** (PUVA)
- Baseline: drug history, ANA if suspicion of lupus, LFT for PUVA, eye check for PUVA
- Photographs, PASI/BSA or VASI

## Equipment
- Calibrated cabin; UV meter; dosimetry software or log book
- UV-blocking goggles for every session
- Genital protection (shields for men), face shield if face not affected
- PUVA: 8-methoxypsoralen tablets; UVA-blocking glasses for after the session

## Procedure step by step
1. **Starting dose (NB-UVB)**: 70% of MED, or by skin type when MED is not done (psoriasis: roughly 0.33 J/cm² for type IV and 0.35 J/cm² for type V). Vitiligo is commonly started at a fixed low dose of about 0.2 J/cm² regardless of type.
2. **Increments**: 10–20% each session if no erythema; hold if mild erythema.
3. **PUVA**: give 8-MOP 0.6 mg/kg orally 1.5–2 hours before exposure with food; start UVA around 1.5–2.5 J/cm² for skin types IV–V (or 70% of MPD); increase by 0.5–1 J/cm² per session; treat twice weekly, not on consecutive days.
4. Patient stands in the centre of the cabin with goggles and genital protection.
5. **Endpoint**: faint, painless erythema the next day (NB-UVB) or at 48–72 h (PUVA, so no dose increase within 72 h of a previous increase).
6. **Missed-dose rules (NB-UVB)**:
- Under 1 week: same dose
- 1–2 weeks: reduce by 25%
- 2–3 weeks: reduce by 50%
- More than 3–4 weeks: restart at the initial dose
7. **Cumulative dose log**: record each session's dose and running total; document the number of treatments.

## Post-procedure care
- PUVA: UVA-blocking glasses for 12–24 hours after psoralen and sun protection on that day
- Emollients; avoid extra sun exposure on treatment days
- Report erythema, blistering or itching

## Complications & management
- Painful erythema: skip until settled; resume at 10–20% lower dose
- Blistering: stop until healed; resume at 50% of the last dose
- Nausea from psoralen: take with food, split dose
- Polymorphic light eruption: reduce dose
- Long-term: photoageing and skin-cancer risk (higher with PUVA, especially beyond about 150–200 treatments)

## Sessions & follow-up
- NB-UVB: 2–3 times weekly; PUVA: twice weekly
- Psoriasis: clearance usually takes 20–30 sessions
- Vitiligo: assess at 3 and 6 months; stop if no repigmentation at 6 months
- Stop at clearance; taper only if relapse risk is high
- Annual skin examination for long courses
